name: Bias-aware technical-assessment anomaly investigation

attribution.legal_posture: First-party platform guidance only; named DPRK incident, allegation, adjudication, and independently measured effectiveness require separate source evidence.

caveats: Appearance, accent, nationality, ethnicity, language, geography, time zone, camera behavior, disability-related behavior, and location require corroboration before any adverse decision.

Automated or platform-generated output is a review prompt. Consequential decisions require documented human review, correction, and appeal, rather than treating the output as a dispositive identity or misconduct determination.
Technical-assessment review should use anonymized initial review where feasible, candidate explanation, multiple-reviewer validation, documented proportional action, and question-leak remediation.

Nervousness, disability, communication style, camera refusal, accent, appearance, language, typing rhythm, geography, and unfamiliar tooling require corroboration before any deception finding. Session recordings and telemetry are sensitive and should be minimized, access-controlled, time-limited, and governed by law and policy. Consequential decisions require candidate feedback, correction, and appeal.
Generic platform documentation is retained as defensive guidance; it supplies context rather than a DPRK incident, attribution, allegation, or measured effectiveness claim.

This record retains no people, personas, accounts, entities, incidents, images, biometric material, identity documents, private data or raw behavioral, camera, code, network, location or device signals.

statements: For suspected technical-assessment or interview manipulation, define prohibited conduct in advance; gather multiple relevant facts; use more than one qualified reviewer where practical; separate an anonymized initial evidence review from identity disclosure when feasible; invite the candidate to explain; record the decision and rationale; and remediate leaked or compromised assessment content. One behavioral, camera, code, network, or location anomaly is insufficient on its own.
limitations: Do not infer deception from nervousness, disability, communication style, camera refusal, accent, appearance, language, typing rhythm, geography, or unfamiliar tooling. Session recordings and telemetry are sensitive and should be minimized, access-controlled, time-limited, and governed by law and policy. Candidate feedback, correction, and appeal are required for consequential decisions.
Generic platform documentation is retained only as defensive guidance, not as a DPRK incident, attribution, allegation, or measured effectiveness claim.
Automated or platform-generated output is a review prompt, not a dispositive identity or misconduct determination; consequential decisions require documented human review, correction, and appeal.
Appearance, accent, nationality, ethnicity, language, geography, time zone, camera behavior, disability-related behavior, and location are not standalone adverse signals.
No people, personas, accounts, entities, incidents, images, biometric material, identity documents, private data, or raw behavioral, camera, code, network, location, or device signals are retained.
